chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Kathīr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Indeed, the first successor upon the face of the earth was Hibat Allah ibn Adam, and there was no Prophet who passed except that he had a successor. The totality of the Prophets were one hundred and twenty thousand Prophets, and among them were five Possessors of Resolve: Nūḥ, Ibrāhīm, Mūsā, ʿĪsā, and Muḥammad عليهم السلام. And indeed, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib was the Hibat Allah for Muḥammad, and he inherited the knowledge of the successors and the knowledge of those who were before him.”

Indeed, Muḥammad inherited the knowledge of those before him from among the Prophets and the Messengers. Upon the pillar of the Throne it is written: ‘Ḥamza is the Lion of Allah and the Lion of His Messenger and the chief of the martyrs,’ and in the crest of the Throne: ‘ʿAlī is the Commander of the Faithful.’

So this is our proof against the one who denies our right and rejects our inheritance. And nothing has prevented us from speaking while certainty is before us; so what proof could be more eloquent than this?”

key_terms.أُولُو الْعَزْمِ: the five prophets of highest resolve and rank
key_terms.الْعَرْشِ: the Throne, indicating exalted heavenly inscription and divine authority
key_terms.حُجَّتُنَا: our proof, meaning decisive evidence for their right
key_terms.عِلْمَ: knowledge, especially the inherited sacred knowledge of prophets and successors
key_terms.مِيرَاثَنَا: our inheritance, referring to the inherited knowledge and authority of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.هِبَةُ اللَّهِ: the gift of Allah; here used as a title of honored succession
key_terms.وَرِثَ: inherited, meaning received divinely transmitted knowledge and authority
key_terms.وَصِيٍّ: a designated successor appointed after a prophet

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the inheritance of knowledge and succession from the prophets to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith presents the continuity of divinely appointed successors from the earliest prophets and places Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام within that sacred line of inheritance. It emphasizes that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and his successors inherit divine knowledge, and it frames the rights and authority of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام as established by heavenly proof.
